newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Banking buy helps Fortis to 30 pct Q1 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Banking buy helps Fortis to 30 pct Q1 profit rise.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis said on Wednesday its first-quarter 1997 profit rose by 30 percent to 204 million ECUs ($233.4 million) from 157 million ECUs in the first three months of 1996.
Fortis said first quarter earnings were boosted by the recently acquired Dutch investment bank MeesPierson and a recovery in the United States.
But it added that operating profits from the insurance sector in Belgium fell, due in part to frost-damage claims.
Fortis said that for the whole of 1997 it expected group net profits and earnings per share of its two parent companies to rise by 10 to 15 percent.
Shares of the parent companies -- Fortis Amev and Fortis AG -- rose to new highs after the higher than expected first quarter results were announced.
Analysts had been expecting the group's first-quarter earnings to rise by about 18 percent.
The reported results showed that net profit from insurance rose by 13 percent to 138 million ECUs while net profit from banking rose 83 percent to 85 million ECUs.
Belgian insurance profits fell as a result of lower earnings from fire insurance and frost damage claims, while life insurance in Belgium produced mixed results.
In the Dutch market, MeesPierson -- acquired from ABN AMRO at the start of this year -- made an immediate positive contribution to earnings, Fortis said.

Operating profits in the United States rose as a result of a powerful recovery in life insurance and a better performance from accident and health insurance, partly because of the disposal of a number of loss-making activities.
-- Wendy Braanker, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000 ($ = 0.874 European Currency Unit ECUs)
